data.title: Run Tyran under Cursor, Copilot, Codex and Antigravity
data.scheduled: deferred — operator time-bound, resumed when the operator has capacity
data.summary: Port Tyran off its Claude Code-only surface. All four rival harnesses now ship a blocking PreToolUse hook, so the mechanisms-not-instructions thesis survives the port. Adopt what already works first; the board states out loud what is only advisory or unavailable per harness.

data.text: Adopt first, enforce second, measure continuously. Phase 1 ships the state layer, skills, agents and rules to three more harnesses with no gate work at all, because 19 of 29 scripts are already harness-free and the skills already satisfy the Agent Skills open standard. Phase 2 extracts a harness descriptor seam with no behaviour change. Phase 3 buys back enforcement, cheapest harness first. Phase 4 measures every contract and takes on Antigravity. The board carries a three-state capability table (ENFORCED / ADVISORY / UNAVAILABLE) at all times, so a mechanism that is only prose under a given harness says so.

data.title: Phase 1 — `tyran init --harness <name>`: generate skills, agents and the rules fence
data.text: Copy skills/*/SKILL.md to .agents/skills/ (read verbatim by all four harnesses; only ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} -> ${TYRAN_ROOT} needs substituting, in 6 of 14 files). Generate agents/*.md into each harness dialect from the single source. Write the rules fence to AGENTS.md rather than CLAUDE.md. New subcommand in bin/tyran.mjs, new adapters/<harness>/ tree.

data.title: Phase 1 — detect the harness and record it in config.yaml with provenance
data.text: scan-repo.mjs learns the repo markers for each harness (.cursor/, .codex/, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .agents/, .claude/). Writes a `harness:` key carrying the fact that produced it and a confidence, exactly as every other inferred value already does. schema.mjs validates the key. Never guesses when two harnesses are both present — it asks.

data.title: Phase 1 — the board Harness panel: three states, never silence
data.text: New tab in board-html.mjs and the same table as text in BOARD.md via project.mjs, so the agent and git surfaces carry it too. One row per capability in exactly three states, each naming its consequence and the operator next step. ENFORCED: the mechanism is live and has been SEEN to refuse. ADVISORY: the rule exists only as prose here, and a model can ignore it. UNAVAILABLE: no data source, the dependent surface is not rendered at all and the panel says why. Extends cost.mjs:29 (gaps are reported, never zeroed) from rows to whole features.

data.title: Phase 2 — scripts/harness.mjs: one frozen descriptor per harness
data.text: The only place a harness-specific name may appear, mirroring the rule tests/unit/agents.test.mjs already pins for model names in tiers:. Each descriptor carries events (canonical -> {nativeName, canBlock, refusalShape, context}), wire (input field map and output shapes), tools (alias map to the canonical verbs write/read/shell/mcp, replacing four scattered tables), paths, failPosture plus the flag that forces it closed, install (registry location and the env var standing in for ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}) and capabilities. Add normalizeInput(harness, raw) returning a frozen canonical payload. A CI test fails on any harness name outside this file.

data.title: Phase 2 — rewire the hook runtime and the nine gates onto canonical fields
data.text: hooks/scripts/hook-io.mjs reads EVENTS and the payload builders from the descriptor; the nine gates under hooks/scripts/ read canonical fields and stop knowing the word Bash. This deletes the duplicate tool tables at policy-gate.mjs:134-144, usage-gate.mjs:101, write-guard.mjs:101-298 and hooks-check.mjs:178-236. NO behaviour change: the whole suite passes with no expectation edits and the projections stay byte-identical under --check. CONSTRAINT: hooks/** is KERNEL in this repo, so an agent session cannot make these edits — they go through an anchored apply-script the human runs, verified against copies first.

data.title: Phase 3 — Copilot and Codex gate adapters (the cheap wins, take them first)
data.text: Both already speak Claude Code hook shape: Copilot/VS Code reads .claude/settings.json natively with PascalCase events and Claude matcher semantics, and Codex mirrors the payload (hook_event_name, hookSpecificOutput, exit-2 deny). The adapter may be a registry emitter and little else. Codex additionally needs its hook-trust onboarding surfaced: hooks must be trusted by hash via /hooks before they fire, so an untrusted hook is an ABSENT gate and must be a board finding, not a footnote.

data.title: Phase 3 — Cursor gate adapter, the proving target, with failClosed: true
data.text: Richest surface (7 blocking events), so it finds the seam design gaps. Map preToolUse + beforeShellExecution + beforeMCPExecution -> policy and secrets gates, beforeReadFile -> the secret-read rule, subagentStop -> evidence gate, stop -> retro gate, sessionStart -> the probe. Cursor hooks default to fail-OPEN, so emit failClosed: true on EVERY gate and have doctor verify the flag is present — without it the gate is decoration, which is precisely the defect hook-io.mjs:5 exists to prevent.

data.title: Phase 3 — doctor --harness, and configured-but-unenforceable becomes an ERROR
data.text: New mode beside --state and --hooks. New finding codes with rows added to the docs/doctor.md severity table in BOTH directions (it is checked against SEVERITY_BY_CODE both ways). The load-bearing rule: `limits: mode: pause` on a harness with no spend.subscriptionWindow FAILS, rather than being silently inert. That exact bug already cost one cycle — usage-source.mjs:5-13 records overnight mode having never once been able to fire.

data.title: Phase 3 — per-harness telemetry: unavailable must never read as zero
data.text: cost.mjs gains per-harness transcript readers (Codex transcript_path in the hook payload, Antigravity transcript.jsonl with a usage block, Copilot events.jsonl with no documented token fields, Cursor only via the Enterprise Admin API). usage-source.mjs, overnight.mjs and statusline.mjs become capability-gated and refuse to be silently inert. overnight.mjs:143-147 shells `claude -p --resume` and needs the per-harness headless equivalent (cursor-agent -p, codex exec, agy -p) or the feature is off and says so.

data.title: Phase 4 — measured hook contracts, one file per harness
data.text: The research behind this initiative is documentation-derived. hooks/HOOK-CONTRACT-MEASURED.md (429 lines disassembled out of the Claude Code binary) is the standard this repo holds itself to, and several findings are surprising enough to need it. Build one echo-hook, register it in each tool, drive deny/allow/ask through it, and write hooks/contracts/<harness>.md in the existing measured format with every unverified cell marked UNMEASURED. A capability may only read ENFORCED on the board once its contract file says measured. Runs alongside Phases 1-3 rather than blocking them.

data.title: Phase 4 — Antigravity, last and least certain
data.text: Thinnest surface of the four: PreToolUse is the only blocking event, so there is no SubagentStop and the evidence contract cannot be enforced — it ships ADVISORY or not at all. Undocumented rules frontmatter keys, undocumented workflows directory, and a plugin manifest with NO version field, which breaks the update path CLAUDE.md names as the most expensive mistake in this repo. A legitimate outcome here is shipping with the board saying what Tyran cannot do under Antigravity.

data.title: Phase 1-4 — documentation on both surfaces, and the claims that CI checks
data.text: Every claim lands in docs/*.md AND site/src/content/docs/*.mdx — they were migrated from each other once and immediately diverged. README.md:211 ("The only requirement is Claude Code >= 2.1") becomes a per-harness table. The README unit-test count is verified by a CI step, not by the suite, so it must be updated with the run own `tests N`. Site cross-links must be relative or the Pages build fails.

data.text: Tyran will support harnesses other than Claude Code. This REVERSES two stated positions: docs/architecture.md:201 ("Native mechanisms only. Built entirely on Claude Code’s plugin surface") and README.md:211 ("The only requirement is Claude Code >= 2.1"). The reversal is justified because the single argument behind them — that only Claude Code can give a gate teeth — stopped being true when Cursor, Copilot, Codex and Antigravity all shipped a blocking PreToolUse hook. video/scripts/team-output.json:10 also records a deliberate "Claude Code only" boundary for the launch video; that copy needs revisiting when this ships.

Portable core with a degraded UI, NOT full parity everywhere and NOT documentation-only. The state layer, journal, projections, board, doctor, policy classification and the CLI run under any harness. Enforcement is mechanical where the harness offers it. A feature with no data source under a harness is not rendered at all. Rejected: attempting full parity via shims (git hooks, wrapper processes, filesystem watchers) — a much larger surface with more ways to be quietly broken, which is the failure class this project exists to prevent.

When a harness cannot enforce a gate, Tyran RUNS and says so loudly rather than refusing to install. Rejected: refusing to run without teeth (excludes users for a purity that the board can express instead) and falling back to git hooks plus CI (moves enforcement to a later boundary while appearing to be the same control, which is worse than an honest advisory).

Phase ordering is ADOPT FIRST. Phase 1 ships skills, agents, the rules fence and the whole state layer to three more harnesses with no gate work at all, and does not wait on the measured contracts of Phase 4. The reason is arithmetic: 19 of 29 scripts and 5 of 9 hook handlers are already harness-free, and the skills already satisfy an open standard, so most of Tyran works out of the box. Blocking that on IDE-by-IDE hook measurement would delay the large, cheap win behind the small, expensive one.

scripts/harness.mjs is the ONLY file in which a harness name or a harness-specific field name may appear, enforced by a CI test. This copies a rule the repo already holds for model names — tiers: is the single place haiku/sonnet/opus/fable may be written, pinned by tests/unit/agents.test.mjs — because the failure it prevents is the same one: a second spelling of the truth that drifts from the first (ADR-21).

A capability reads ENFORCED on the board only once the gate has been SEEN REFUSING under that harness, never once it has merely been registered. Registration without a measured refusal is the exact shape of the defect hook-io.mjs:5 was written against: a control that looks like it works and cannot say no. Until then the row reads ADVISORY.

Cursor is the proving target for the descriptor seam, because its 7 blocking events are the widest surface and will expose the design gaps. But Copilot and Codex gate adapters are taken OPPORTUNISTICALLY FIRST where they fall out cheaply, since both already speak Claude Code hook shape. Proving the hard case and shipping the easy ones are not the same decision and should not be sequenced as if they were.

data.claim: All four rival harnesses now ship a blocking PreToolUse-class hook that can return deny and stop a tool call before it executes. This is no longer a Claude Code differentiator, and it is the fact the whole initiative rests on.
data.confidence: documented, not yet measured — see T-10

data.claim: GitHub Copilot in VS Code reads .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json NATIVELY, with PascalCase event names and Claude matcher semantics (setting: chat.hookFilesLocations). Copilot deliberately accepts Claude Code hook format, which makes the Copilot gate adapter close to free.

OpenAI Codex mirrors the Claude Code hook payload shape: hook_event_name, matcher groups, hookSpecificOutput with permissionDecision deny, and exit code 2 as an alternative deny. Config at ~/.codex/hooks.json, <repo>/.codex/hooks.json, or inline [hooks] in config.toml; plugins ship hooks/hooks.json. Events include SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStop and Stop.

CURSOR HOOKS DEFAULT TO FAIL-OPEN. Each handler takes an optional failClosed flag and it is false by default, so a hook that crashes, times out or is missing lets the action through. Any Cursor config Tyran emits must set failClosed: true on every gate, and doctor must verify the flag — otherwise Tyran would ship the precise defect hook-io.mjs:5 exists to prevent.
data.confidence: documented, not yet measured — highest-priority item for T-10

data.claim: Codex will not run a non-managed hook until it has been reviewed and trusted BY HASH via the /hooks command. A third party cannot drop a hooks.json into a repo and have it fire. An untrusted Tyran hook under Codex is an ABSENT gate, so it needs an onboarding step in the installer and a doctor finding when the state is untrusted. Escape hatch --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust exists; managed hooks from MDM or requirements.toml skip review.

Anthropic’s Agent Skills format is now an open standard read verbatim by Cursor, GitHub Copilot/VS Code, Codex and Antigravity from .agents/skills/. Spec is folder + SKILL.md with frontmatter name (<=64 chars, lowercase-hyphens, must match the directory) and description (<=1024, required); optional scripts/, references/, assets/. Tyran’s 14 skills already comply — they are single SKILL.md files with a description. This is the largest free win in the whole initiative.

AGENTS.md is now governed by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation (formed Dec 2025, anchored by MCP, goose and AGENTS.md; 150+ members, 60k+ repos). Supported by Codex, Cursor, VS Code/Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Devin, Zed, Warp, Aider, goose, opencode and others. It is the natural replacement target for the CLAUDE.md rules fence that mistakes.mjs writes.

ANTIGRAVITY DOES NOT DOCUMENT AGENTS.md ANYWHERE. Its documented global context file is ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md, with workspace rules in .agents/rules/ (12,000 character limit per file). It is the one tool of the four that has not joined the AGENTS.md convention, so the rules-fence target must be resolved per harness rather than assumed.
data.source: https://antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows/ — checked rules, workflows, ide/settings and agent-settings pages plus site-scoped search

data.claim: 19 of 29 scripts carry ZERO Claude-specific references: journal, project, board, board-daemon, board-html, knowledge, mistakes, tiers, answer, stop-check, migrate, yaml-lite, yaml-patch, invisible, scan-control-chars, cli-args, desc-budget, keepawake, ensure-gitleaks. So do 5 of the 9 hook handlers — write-guard, secrets-gate, retro-gate, pre-compact and board-refresh. The state layer, the projections, the board and the policy classification are already portable.
data.source: grep for CLAUDE_[A-Z_]* across scripts/ hooks/ skills/ agents/ templates/ in this repo

data.claim: bin/tyran.mjs already publishes 19 subcommands on npm as @jjanczur/tyran, described in package.json as "for CI and terminals outside Claude Code", delegating verbatim to scripts/ with the exit code preserved. Any harness with a shell tool can therefore drive the entire journal, projection, board, doctor, knowledge, tiers, answer-sheet and STOP-brake surface TODAY via npx, with no adapter written. The harness-free half is already built, tested and shipped.

The Claude coupling is narrow and enumerable: the hook wire protocol lives in ONE file (hook-io.mjs); registration format plus ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (53 refs, 6 of 14 skills); four duplicated tool-name tables (policy-gate.mjs:134-144, usage-gate.mjs:101, write-guard.mjs:101-298, hooks-check.mjs:178-236); the Claude matcher predicate transcribed from the binary (hooks-check.mjs:210, pinned to PLATFORM_VERSION); transcript and usage formats (cost.mjs, usage-source.mjs, statusline.mjs); `claude -p --resume` (overnight.mjs:143-147); the CLAUDE.md rules fence (mistakes.mjs:65,391,844); and the manifests plus asset frontmatter.

Per-token cost is NOT uniformly available. Codex exposes transcript_path in every hook payload; Antigravity writes transcript.jsonl with a usage block (input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cache_read_tokens); Copilot writes ~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl with NO documented token fields; Cursor exposes token counts and chargedCents only through the Enterprise-gated Admin API (POST /teams/filtered-usage-events). So the board Spend surface must hide under Cursor and Copilot rather than render zeros.

Subscription usage windows are Claude-only. usage-source.mjs reads ~/.claude.json cachedUsageUtilization, and no equivalent was found for any other harness. The overnight wind-down (limits: mode: pause) therefore cannot fire elsewhere — which must be a doctor ERROR rather than silence, because usage-source.mjs:5-13 records this exact bug already happening once: the gate failed open, nothing said so, and overnight mode was silently inert.
data.source: scripts/usage-source.mjs:1-45 · absence confirmed across the four harness doc sets

data.claim: Antigravity is the weakest target. Only five hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop) and ONLY PreToolUse can block — so there is no SubagentStop and the evidence contract, Tyran’s headline mechanism, cannot be enforced there at all. Its plugin manifest has only $schema, name and description with NO version field, so there is no documented update semantics — which breaks the release discipline CLAUDE.md names as the most expensive mistake in this repo.

Cursor has the richest hook surface of all four, Claude Code included: ~20 events of which 7 can block — preToolUse, subagentStart, beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile, beforeTabFileRead, beforeSubmitPrompt. beforeReadFile can rewrite content before it reaches the model, and sessionStart can inject env and additional_context. Project hooks load automatically in cloud agents (command-type only).

UNCONFIRMED, and must not be built on until T-10 measures it. Antigravity: AGENTS.md support, rules frontmatter key names, the workflows directory path, plugin versioning, and whether the global root is ~/.gemini/config/ or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ (the IDE and CLI docs contradict each other). Codex: official documentation of the ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl path (community-reported only). Cursor: whether --output-format stream-json carries token or cost fields, and the current docs page for .cursor/commands/ (skills appear to have superseded it). Copilot: per-token cost fields inside events.jsonl.
data.source: research agent, this session — explicitly reported as not confirmable from official docs

data.next_steps: Nothing is scheduled. When the operator has time, start with T-1/T-2/T-3 (Phase 1), which need no gate work and deliver most of Tyran to Cursor, Codex and Copilot. T-4 (the descriptor seam) is the highest value-per-risk code change and can land alone. T-5 requires a HUMAN edit: hooks/** is KERNEL in this repo, so an agent session cannot touch the runtime or the gates — use an anchored apply-script verified against copies first. T-10 (measured contracts) runs alongside, never blocking.
